questions.question: Why are visible input tokens useful even when their output positions are excluded from the loss?
options: They supply context to predictions at selected positions through the encoder.
Unselected output logits still receive a nonzero direct cross-entropy gradient.
Excluding a position from the loss also masks its key and value vectors out of attention.
questions.explanation: The mask controls the supervised outputs, while attention controls how input context influences them.
optionFeedback: The mask controls the supervised outputs, while attention controls how input context influences them.
Only selected targets contribute direct loss, but other input tokens still provide context through attention. Distinguish input masking from loss masking.
A loss mask selects scored positions; it does not remove keys or values from attention. Test those masks independently.
